The best translation schools and universities in Belgium

May 8, 2017
Education | Students

Where do Belgium's translators and interpreters train? The profession needs solid foundations, and the country's universities offer a wide choice of degrees in French, Dutch and several other languages.

Belgium has three official languages, Dutch, French and German, so translation training sits at the heart of its higher education. Brussels, Ghent, Leuven, Antwerp, Liège and Mons all have programmes.

This overview covers the main university programmes in French-speaking and Dutch-speaking Belgium, and explains what it means for UK businesses that need translators who know the Belgian market.

How translation training works in Belgium

In French-speaking Belgium, the 2013 higher education reform known as the Paysage decree, or Marcourt decree, was followed by a 2014 decree that brought translation and interpreting schools into universities. Today a bachelor's degree normally takes three years and a master's takes two years, or 120 ECTS credits.

Flanders has long taught translation and interpreting within its universities. Programme length and language combinations differ, so check each university's current course page before you apply.

Translation schools in Brussels

Marie Haps Faculty of Translation and Interpreting, Université Saint-Louis and UCLouvain

Marie Haps trains translators and interpreters in the European quarter of Brussels, close to the EU institutions. Since 2015 it has been a faculty of Université Saint-Louis, Bruxelles, which is part of UCLouvain.

The bachelor's degree stays in Brussels, while the master's is taught by UCLouvain at Louvain-la-Neuve. The school also offers a bachelor's in sign language translation and interpreting, launched in 2014 and described as the only one of its kind in Belgium.

Institut supérieur de traducteurs et interprètes (ISTI), Université libre de Bruxelles

ISTI is part of the ULB Faculty of Letters, Translation and Communication. It offers a bachelor's in translation and interpreting, separate master's degrees in translation and in interpreting, and a certificate for sworn translators and interpreters.

ULB students translate and interpret from a foreign language into French, so they graduate as specialists in their mother tongue.

Translation schools in Flanders

Department of Translation, Interpreting and Communication, Ghent University

Ghent University teaches a bachelor's in applied language studies, followed by master's degrees in translation, interpreting and multilingual communication. Students traditionally take Dutch as their first language and add two other languages.

The department also researches language technology, which matters as machine translation becomes part of the professional workflow.

KU Leuven Faculty of Arts, including the Antwerp campus and CETRA

KU Leuven teaches translation and interpreting across its Antwerp, Brussels and Leuven campuses. The Antwerp master's in translation holds the European Master's in Translation label from the European Commission.

CETRA, the Centre for Translation Studies in Leuven, is one of the best-known research centres in the field.

University of Antwerp, applied linguistics

The University of Antwerp runs a master's in translation and a master's in interpreting. Its translation master's also carries the European Master's in Translation label.

Translation schools in Wallonia

Université de Liège and Haute École de la Ville de Liège

Liège runs its translation and interpreting courses jointly with the Haute École de la Ville de Liège. Students study at both institutions during the bachelor's before they specialise in translation or interpreting at master's level.

Faculty of Translation and Interpreting, École d'Interprètes Internationaux, Université de Mons

The École d'Interprètes Internationaux at Mons offers a master's in interpreting and a master's in translation. The translation master has three options: advanced translation, translation in an intercultural context and multidisciplinary translation.

Louvain School of Translation and Interpreting, UCLouvain

UCLouvain should not be confused with KU Leuven, which is a separate Dutch-speaking university. The Louvain School teaches in French and runs the master's programmes at Louvain-la-Neuve, while the bachelor's is taught in Brussels at Marie Haps.

What this means for UK businesses

Belgium's translators are trained to a high academic standard, but you still need to choose the right language variety. Belgian Dutch and Belgian French both differ from the versions used in the Netherlands and France, and the right choice depends on whether you sell in Flanders, Wallonia or Brussels.

If you plan to trade with Belgium, read about the translation market in Belgium and the services we offer in Dutch, French and German.

Frequently asked questions

Where can you study translation in Belgium?

You can study translation at universities in Brussels, Ghent, Leuven, Antwerp, Liège, Mons and Louvain-la-Neuve. Among them are ULB, Ghent University, KU Leuven, the University of Antwerp, ULiège, UMONS and UCLouvain. Each teaches different language combinations.

How long does a translation degree take in Belgium?

In French-speaking Belgium, a bachelor's takes three years and a master's usually takes two years. Check the course page for the exact length at each university, because Flemish programmes are structured differently.

Which Belgian universities hold the European Master's in Translation label?

The European Commission lists the KU Leuven Antwerp master's in translation among its labelled programmes. The University of Antwerp also states that its master's in translation holds the label. The Commission publishes the full list of members.

Do Belgian translators work into English?

Most professional translators work into their mother tongue. ULB students, for example, translate from foreign languages into French. For English content, a native English translator is the safer choice.

Can a UK business hire translators with Belgian training?

Yes, and many graduates work across Europe. BeTranslated matches your project with native translators for Dutch, French and German, including Belgian variants where the market requires it. Send your brief and we will recommend the right linguist.
